messages:
Evan (mobile): Heads up — QA on iOS is seeing a bunch of 401 invalid_api_key after the 1.2.2 release. Only affects iOS builds. Works fine from Postman and Android. Any ideas?

Alicia (support): Can you paste an example request/headers + the server log snippet?

Evan (mobile): Here's a redacted curl and the server response we get in logs:
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Apikey acct:ABCD1234EFGH5678IJKL9012MNOP3456\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_api_key\",
  \"message\": \"api key not found\"
}
```
I replaced the real key but note the header contains `acct:` prefix. When paste from the device it seems to include that.

Chris (eng-infra): Interesting — `acct:` looks like an iOS Keychain/AutoFill prefix. iOS Password AutoFill sometimes returns items with an `acct:` or `user:` prefix depending on how the entry was created. Can you check the raw header bytes/length?

Evan (mobile): Yep, we logged header length. Expected 32 chars for keys; we see length 37. Example debug output: `auth_header_raw=\"acct:ABCD1234EFGH5678IJKL9012MNOP3456\" len=37`. If I manually remove `acct:` and resend it works.

Ben (support): Has QA definitely not manually typed? Could the provisioning script have created the key entry in Keychain with an `acct` attribute?

Evan (mobile): QA says they used the system autofill prompt. The saved credential in iOS passwords shows the key in the \"Password\" field, but when you "Fill Password" the autofill sometimes prepends `acct:` (weird). Repro steps:
1) Save API key into iOS Passwords as a new login (username blank, password = API key)
2) In our app's settings, tap the API key field and tap the autofill item
3) The inserted text is `acct:<key>` instead of `<key>`

Chris (eng-infra): We should fix in the client SDK to normalize keys on input (trim common prefixes and non-alphanumeric chars). Server-side lenient acceptors are risky. I'll draft a tiny change in the mobile SDK to strip leading `acct:` / `user:` / `username:` (only if overall length matches expected after strip).

Maria (prod infra): Can you capture a few raw requests (no redaction) from a repro device to confirm there's no other corruption (null bytes, unicode)? Attach logs if possible. We'll avoid server change unless unavoidable.

Evan (mobile): Attached raw header dump in the thread (private log). I verified it's plain ascii `acct:` followed by the exact 32-char base key. No hidden chars. iOS version tested: 16.4 and 16.5 beta. Happens on both.

Alicia (support): Customer-facing note draft: "If you're using iOS AutoFill to insert API keys, the system may prepend a credential prefix (e.g. `acct:`). If you see 401s, try pasting the key manually or update to our next client patch which normalizes the value." Want to run by legal?

Chris (eng-infra): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mobile-sdk/pull/642 — small sanitizer on input + unit tests. Will default to sanitize only in the settings UI and SDK constructor, not on every runtime header to minimize axe surface.

Ben (support): Short-term workaround for customers: Instruct to long-press the autofill suggestion and choose "Copy Password" then paste (that seems to avoid the prefix) or manually remove `acct:`.

Evan (mobile): Merged SDK patch to our internal build, bumped to 1.2.3. Rolling to QA now.

Evan (mobile): QA confirmed: 1.2.3 no longer sends `acct:` and the customer reports requests are succeeding again :tada:

Alicia (support): Closing the incident after follow-up email sent. Will include the workaround + SDK 1.2.3 in the KB article.

Chris (eng-infra): Note for infra: We'll add a short-lived diagnostic metric to count header lengths that are > expected to spot similar oddities going forward.
